dedupe_keys.name: høje taastrup pit thermal energy storage use case and measurement

description: This case study presents the large pit thermal energy storage at Høje Taastrup in Denmark, which is integrated into district heating networks to make efficient use of waste heat and to balance heat over the week. It was prepared by Jianhua Fan of the Technical University of Denmark and published on Zenodo as a presentation. It highlights how detailed monitoring and simulation with TRNSYS were used to validate the storage's performance, analyse heat losses and thermal stratification, and optimise operation on the basis of reliable measured data. Coverage is the Høje Taastrup storage and its connection to the heat networks. The material is one PDF of about 3 MB accessible online on Zenodo (April 2026) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the record gives a short summary, the slides do not publish the underlying measurement data, and detailed results must be read from the PDF. It shows operations and control analysis of seasonal and weekly heat storage, with simulation uses in storage optimisation and digital twins of heat networks. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day. A separate study of the same installation reports annual energy and exergy efficiencies of 89 and 75 percent and assesses stratification and liner temperature resistance. These are study-specific outcomes; exact annual sample overlap with the presentation is unknown.
